newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-DOUBLE FAILURE FOR SLATER, BUT NSW IN CHARGE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DOUBLE FAILURE FOR SLATER, BUT NSW IN CHARGE.

text.p: Former Australia opener Michael Slater fell cheaply for the second time in as many days in a Sheffield Shield match on Saturday to virtually end his chances of a recall for the fourth test against West Indies.
Slater, dropped from the national side at the end of last year, was trapped lbw for just four to follow his first innings score of three for New South Wales against South Australia in Adelaide.
But New South Wales took control of the four-day match by dismissing South Australia for just 137 in reply to their 415.
Captain Greg Matthews chose not to enforce the follow-on, giving Slater the chance to impress national selectors ahead of the test in Adelaide later this month.
New South Wales will resume the third day on 14 for one.
In Perth, opener Michael Hussey scored his third first class century as Western Australia took the upper hand in their match against Victoria.
Hussey stroked 147 as Western Australia reached 329 for three at the close on the second day in reply to Victoria's 332.
